title: identity.api_key.revoked payload
description: The `data` payload of the `identity.api_key.revoked` event: a scoped machine credential stopped being honoured. Two fields, and the omissions are the contract. There is NO `revoke_reason`, and the reason is the same one the publisher keeps for the OIDC revocation: a reason is operator-facing context typed by a human at a support call site, its set of values is open, it is not a fact about the credential, and a field whose values vary per operator is a field every consumer learns to ignore. It stays on the row, where identity's own support reads it, which is a different consumer with a different need — and note the spelling: the column is `revoke_reason` and nothing on the bus carries it. There is no `last_used_at` either, which is the more interesting of the two omissions: whether a withdrawn credential was in use is the single most useful thing an operator wants afterwards, and it is a join away on a row that still exists. Putting it on the event freezes one reading of it in a store with a different lifetime. And the catalog calls this the event for an expiry as well as a withdrawal; identity has no sweeper, so only the withdrawal is emitted today. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

account_id.description: The account the credential acted on. Present for the same reason it is on `identity.api_key.created`: the subject is the credential, and a consumer auditing an account's credentials correlates here.

revoked_by.description: The user who withdrew it, and NOT necessarily the user who minted it: an owner of an account may withdraw a credential another owner minted, because a live credential in an account is the account's problem rather than one member's. Never null — the publisher refuses the revocation rather than writing a row with no actor. This is the `actor`, which is the one thing the envelope's `subject` is not: the subject is the credential that stopped working.
